pr_title: [release/6.0-rc1] HTTP/3: Use new QuicStream.ReadsCompleted property in transport
pr_body:
Fixes #35399
Backport of #35476 to release/6.0-rc1

/cc @JamesNK

## Customer Impact

HTTP/3 GET requests will unexpected write logs that the request body has not been read. Fixed by this change.

## Testing

Unit and functional tests.

## Risk

Low. Only changes QUIC usage in Kestrel. The only user of this API is HTTP/3 which is in preview in .NET 6.

review_comments: Why bother, we're already in a state machine

Because the `ValueTask` needs to get converted to a `ValueTask<FlushResult>`. The goal isn't to avoid a state machine in the parent method, it's to avoid the one in the local method.

(the reason to convert to `ValueTask<FlushResult>` is so `CompleteAsync` and `FlushAsync` use the same code path)

It makes more sense if you see more of the method:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/ef7c86a56b8678157a8a523260b661f86090313b/src/Servers/Kestrel/Transport.Quic/src/Internal/QuicStreamContext.cs#L190-L227
